decision: No-Go for a new security experiment or parameter/amplitude search. Keep the source-level many-to-one fact as an implementation diagnostic.
execution_chain: native raw action latent -> mean decoder -> inverse min-max -> env.step continuous 7-vector
six arm coordinates -> OSC input clip -> pose goals -> torque controller -> actuator control
gripper coordinate -> sign -> internal current_action update -> actuator control

source_findings.gripper_many_to_one: For finite nonzero values with identical sign, identical six arm coordinates and identical initial physical/controller state, the gripper format_action recurrence and its resulting actuator control are identical at each physics substep. This is a code-derived property; no new simulator replay was run.
source_findings.arm_clipping: Different commands outside a common input bound can map to the same scaled OSC delta. No arm command in the existing candidate logs crosses the [-1,1] controller bounds.
source_findings.torque_saturation_limit: Equal clipped torques at one instant do not prove equal full-chunk execution because distinct goals and evolving dynamics can diverge later.
source_findings.wrapper_state_limit: recent_actions stores raw commands. Aliases therefore cannot be described as preserving all software/controller-associated buffers. Source search found this buffer written by the robot path but not read by the audited physical dynamics or model observation codec.
source_findings.native_entry_limit: In the evaluated native path candidate latents are generated internally, then consumed directly by forecast and value. Changing their gripper amplitude requires added intermediate action/latent write access or a new candidate-proposal interface; no attacker-accessible native entry was established.
source_findings.statistical_limit: Execution equivalence does not guarantee observational conditional independence or in-support model inputs. A forecast difference after rewriting an action representation is not by itself prediction error, native decision harm, or a security attack.

log_recomputation.source: All recorded N2 candidates in all 30 completed Clean episode chunk logs; includes candidates in the final partially executed chunk.
log_recomputation.canonical_mapping: C(a) = concat(clip(a[0:6], -1, 1), sign(a[6])); sign(0) = 0. No new actions are sampled, executed, or submitted to a model.
log_recomputation.equality_definition: Entire 16x7 C(action) flattened row-major, packed as 112 little-endian IEEE754 binary64 values; exact byte comparison, no tolerance.
log_recomputation.scope: This compares a sufficient controller-command equivalence representation. Zero matches does not rule out all state-dependent physical aliases or prove future trajectories unequal.
log_recomputation.independence_limit: 232 pairs are correlated policy chunks from 30 episodes, not independent experimental trials; no significance test or population claim.

normalization_stats.limit: Min/max metadata alone does not establish the training distribution of gripper amplitudes or joint observation-action support.

possible_exact_verification_not_executed: Fresh fixed-seed prefix replay, same complete physical/controller starting state, fixed candidate arm coordinates and same gripper signs.
At every physics substep compare sim.data.ctrl, gripper.current_action, OSC goals, qpos/qvel and physical observations with dtype/shape/bytes; separately disclose raw-action log-buffer changes.
Do not infer equivalence from final images or endpoint state alone.

prior_evidence_boundary.wav: The earlier alias mechanism was already rejected as an OOD/action-equivalence diagnostic with no native controller harm; this audit supplies no distinct threat entry.
prior_evidence_boundary.cosmos_copy_alias: Canonical/reverse redundant-copy interventions already produced zero ranking flips and zero success losses in valid windows; do not reinterpret those negative results as support for a stronger operation.

next_action: Stop. No new model, environment, API, parameter, magnitude, or seed search authorized by this feasibility audit.

sources.finding: Native NVIDIA copied codec averages raw action-latent copies and applies inverse min-max without clipping or gripper binarization.

Native best-of-N internally generates raw action latent, conditions forecast on it, predicts value, then selects its decoded physical actions. No external candidate-replacement entry is exposed by this evaluated path.
Evaluated runner uses LIBERO OffScreenRenderEnv and executes decoded continuous actions directly; physical success comes from environment check_success.
Default Panda, OSC_POSE, default gripper; forwards actions to environment.
Seven-dimensional OSC_POSE actions are forwarded; task termination is checked from environment success.
Gripper update uses sign(action) with speed 0.01 and clips internal current_action to [-1,1]. Same nonzero sign produces identical update arithmetic from identical current_action.
format_action output is rescaled and written to sim.data.ctrl at gripper actuators.

Arm and gripper commands split; controller goal is updated on policy step; torques clipped and gripper controls applied. recent_actions.push(action) stores raw command, so full wrapper state is not identical for an alias.
scale_action clips command to controller input bounds before affine scaling.
Fixed-impedance OSC uses scaled action to update pose goals. Torque saturation alone does not establish equal future controller goals.
OSC_POSE input bounds are [-1,1], fixed impedance, delta control, no position/orientation limits or interpolation.
Each policy action is applied across all physics substeps; exact execution comparison must cover all these controls, not only final endpoints.
Different AlphaBrain evaluator clips normalized actions. This is not the NVIDIA codec used by the audited Clean30 runner; do not conflate execution paths.
Earlier WAV alias diagnostic was rejected as ordinary OOD/action-equivalence generalization without an attacker operation or native controller harm; historical review novelty score 2/10.

Prior redundant-copy canonical/reverse interventions have small mixed-sign RGB error effects and zero ranking flips or actual success losses in all valid windows; distinct tested representation operation, not evidence for gripper-amplitude harm.
